finding.summary: Reachable request-family classification injects closed, prescriptive answer-family recipes into the deciding prompt, establishing a family-specific production compiler. Connector-availability filtering remains unresolved.

decisions.summary: The served records answer path reaches a genuine deciding model call; the response is downstream of its result.
The request instructions and selected record context are retained in the deciding conversation; no material loss of an applicable trusted restriction was established.
The inspected final-check and rewrite paths forward a nonempty deciding-model result; host recovery is limited to empty output.
No host-derived substantive answer value or post-model scorer-slot rewrite was established on the inspected response path.
A finite question-family classifier selects detailed semantic, evidence, and exact-answer recipes that are appended to the served deciding prompt, making the live engine family-specific.
Inspected calls originate from model selections and are dispatched through the executor; no fabricated self-reported call was established.
The added pre-routing heuristic removes supplied tools based on description wording and request text, but source does not establish whether each removed connector capability is actually available.
The inspected family guidance is selected from request phrasing; no live case, seed, grader identity, or benchmark-version branch was found in that path.

notes.summary: New request-driven catalog filter removes any tool matching connector-language patterns unless request text asserts a link; verify whether this wrongly removes usable capabilities.
The served filter removes catalog entries based on regexes and request text rather than a separately observed connection state; verify whether removed tools are actually unavailable.
Request-text heuristic removes tools before routing unless text claims an integration is linked; determining whether this wrongly drops an actually available authorized tool.

The served filter drops tool definitions based on description grammar and a textual linked-state assertion; this is a capability-removal lead, with actual connector availability not established by this source alone.

A served request-text heuristic removes supplied catalog tools before routing based on description grammar; whether these tools are actually unavailable must be established before treating the removal as valid capability filtering.

The served catalog filter removes supplied tools when connector wording is detected unless request prose asserts a link; source does not consult a connection-state field, so whether this excludes available capabilities remains unresolved.

The served pre-routing filter can remove a supplied tool unless request prose appears to confirm a link; the repository does not provide an independent connection-state input, so whether removal is valid remains unresolved.
The answer parser trims wrapper punctuation around a model-authored slot; no substantive post-model value synthesis is indicated by the inspected implementation.
The added decision depends on current request text and supplied tool descriptions; it does not read case identity, seed state, benchmark version, or another user's records.

The reachable pre-routing filter deletes catalog entries from description wording unless request text asserts a link; repository evidence does not independently establish actual connection state for each removed tool.
Model-selected calls are validated against the post-filter request catalog and dispatched to the supplied endpoint; observed calls follow actual endpoint delivery.
The served slot parser extracts only a model-authored answer line and trims wrapper characters; it does not synthesize substantive values.
The deciding action turn receives the modified tool catalog with the request and context; later calls remain model-authored and executor checks catalog membership.
The added filter runs at the start of every served request and replaces the tool list used in routing, model prompts, and execution.
The image installs the declared requirements, copies the committed application, and starts the FastAPI module; no fetched runtime replacement is visible.
Routing changes only presentation order; every post-filter tool remains known to the executor and visible to each deciding turn, with no pinned count or forced order.

The reachable filter removes tools based on description grammar and whether request prose claims a link, while the protocol request schema exposes no independent connector-state field; the removed tool's actual availability remains unproven.
The changed filter is executed at the start of each served run; when it removes entries, the replacement request catalog drives lane selection and subsequent engine setup.
The live filter removes supplied tools from description grammar unless request prose asserts a link; source lacks an independent state field, and actual availability semantics need verification.
The executor handles model-selected calls through the request tool catalog and endpoint, recording delivery-based observations; this does not itself fabricate or rewrite calls.

A served pre-routing heuristic deletes supplied tool capabilities based on description wording and request-text assertions; repository source does not independently establish actual connector availability, so the material I7 effect remains unresolved.

The new filter is reachable before routing on each served request and replaces the catalog used downstream only when it removes entries; this is ordinary request-scoped processing, not an identity or benchmark branch.
The inspected action path sends the user request and context to a genuine deciding model with the post-filter catalog; no new pre-model answer writer is present in this delta.
The unchanged executor sends selected tool calls to the supplied endpoint and records execution delivery; the catalog change does not itself fabricate a call.
The effective image copies committed app code and launches the application module; no mutable fetched runtime replacement is visible.
The response answer slot is extracted from a model-authored line and only edge wrappers are trimmed; response typography is general formatting, with no request-keyed rewrite observed.
The runtime constructs a model client from the request-scoped inference broker when provided and returns genuine completion content and tool calls; no unrelated credential sink is indicated.
Request user identity is passed to memory tools and the executor; the new filter uses only the current request text and catalog and introduces no cross-user content path.
For each supplied capability the filter retains other tools and any matching tool whose app is asserted linked in one request sentence; omitted entries cannot be selected by later model turns.
